hook: Yoshua Bengio has spent his career pushing neural networks from a marginal idea into the foundation of modern AI, and more recently has turned much of his attention to the risks that AI now poses. Born in Paris and raised in Canada, he earned a PhD in computer science from McGill University before joining the Universite de Montreal, where he has been a professor since the early 1990s. His 2003 paper A Neural Probabilistic Language Model helped establish the use of learned word representations in language modeling, an idea that became central to later large language models, and in 2014 he co-authored the paper introducing generative adversarial networks with Ian Goodfellow and others. He founded Mila, the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute, building it into one of the world's largest academic centers for deep learning research, and in 2016 co-founded the AI startup Element AI. In 2018 he shared the ACM A.M. Turing Award with Yann LeCun and Geoffrey Hinton for his contributions to deep learning. In recent years he has chaired the International AI Safety Report and, in June 2025, launched LawZero, a nonprofit research organization focused on building safe, non-agentic AI systems.
